subject: Proposed performance improvement plan — Priya Natarajan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed performance improvement plan — Priya Natarajan

Hi team,

I wanted to loop you in early before I present anything to Priya. Over the past 6 months weve documented repeated misses on delivery (see attached performance-logs.csv) and two coaching conversations (Jan 14, Feb 10). I drafted a PIP to make expectations explicit and provide a clear 60-day improvement window. The draft is attached (pip-draft-marcus-v1.docx).

Key points I'm proposing:
- Objective: reduce incident introduction rate by 40% and meet weekly SLAs consistently.
- Duration: 60 days with weekly checkpoints and a formal review at day 30 and day 60.
- Manager support: weekly 1:1s, paired work sessions, and specific training resources.
- Consequence: failure to show sustained improvement may lead to role change or separation.

I want to make sure the language is HR- and legally-sound (especially the consequence phrasing), and that we follow the correct notification timeline. Proposed next steps:
1) HR: review template and required documentation for the file.
2) Legal: quick scan for wording that could be construed as prescriptive or punitive.
3) Director: confirm alignment with team-level headcount plan and potential backfill approach.

Please review the draft and the logs. Happy to take edits inline or we can combine into a final HR-approved document by Tuesday 3/24 end of day.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Engineering Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pip-draft-marcus-v1.docx (docx), performance-logs.csv (csv)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed performance improvement plan — Priya Natarajan

Thanks Marcus for the thorough summary and for attaching the logs. I read the draft and added a few HR-standard clauses that we always include so the employee understands support resources and appeal steps. Attached: pip-hr-template.docx (this includes our standard language on accommodations and reasonable adjustments).

Edits I recommend (high level):
- Tone down the "consequence" paragraph to "possible role change" rather than an explicit separation timeline. HR prefers progressive language and a clear remediation path.
- Add a section documenting prior coaching conversations (dates + coaches) so the file is audit-ready.
- Confirm whether you want the PIP to be 45 vs 60 days; I generally recommend 60 for technical ramp given backlog alignment.

I flagged two items in the draft where a manager statement could be interpreted as an ultimatum; those should be softened or substantiated with measurable examples.

If Legal can review the changes today, we can finalize a version to share with Priya's lead and schedule a private 1:1 for the kickoff.

Lauren Bishop
HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pip-hr-template.docx (docx)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed performance improvement plan — Priya Natarajan

Thanks for the draft and context. Ive done a quick legal pass and attached notes (pip-legal-notes.pdf). High-level points:

1) Neutral, fact-based language: remove subjective adjectives that cannot be corroborated (e.g., "consistently underperforming"). Replace with specific missed commitments and dates.
2) Avoid implied timelines tied to separation; state that failure to meet the plans objectives "may result in further personnel action subject to applicable company policy." That is less final and defensible.
3) Confidentiality and records: add language specifying who will have access to the PIP document and how it will be stored. This mitigates potential disclosure issues.

Also note: if Priya has any protected accommodation needs on record (I checked our HRIS, none flagged), we should still ask the employee if any accommodations are needed before finalizing.

If you want, I can redline directly into your draft. From a timeline standpoint, please allow 24 hours for a redline + second review; if you need a faster turnaround I can prioritize.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Counsel, Employment
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pip-legal-notes.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed performance improvement plan — Priya Natarajan

Thanks Lauren and Tessa  this is helpful. Ive accepted the HR wording suggestions and will incorporate your legal phrasing in the consequence and confidentiality sections. I agree 60 days is appropriate.

Tessa: please do a redline into the attached draft if you can prioritize today; I need final sign-off before I schedule the private kickoff with Priya. Ill also add the coaching conversation notes and the concrete success metrics (examples below) so theres no ambiguity:
- No more than 1 regression per 2-week sprint attributable to the individuals changes.
- 95% pass rate on the automated pre-merge checks for their owned components.
- Completion of assigned training modules within first 30 days.

Markus: Im proposing we do a private manager-employee kickoff on Wed 3/25 in the morning and copy HR to the document after the meeting. If you prefer a different cadence or want to be present, let me know.

Quote of Tessas note:
> If Priya has any protected accommodation needs on record (I checked our HRIS, none flagged), we should still ask the employee if any accommodations are needed before finalizing.

Ill update the attached doc and resend.

Marcus

Marcus, thanks for taking ownership here and for the clear metrics. I reviewed the summary and am comfortable with the 60-day plan and the proposed objectives, provided HR and Legal sign off on final language. A few quick asks from my side:

- Please ensure the PIP includes an explicit manager action item list (scheduled 1:1s, paired sessions, who will provide code review support). That helps demonstrate active manager support during the period.
- Before sending, hold a private 30-minute calibration call with me so were aligned on tone and potential next steps if the plan does not lead to improvement. I wont be present for the kickoff meeting with Priya but I want to be briefed immediately after.
- If separation becomes the direction, coordinate with Finance on final comp calculations; notify me earlier so I can approve.

If HR and Legal can confirm sign-off today Ill consider this approved from a headcount/planning perspective.
